summary: This lecture page details the computational challenges of training Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), specifically the graph expansion problem where receptive fields grow exponentially with depth. It compares three optimization strategies: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Batch Gradient Descent, and Mini-batch Gradient Descent, highlighting the trade-offs in memory usage, convergence stability, and computational efficiency. The page introduces GraphSAGE as a solution for scalable training through random neighborhood sampling and discusses graph partitioning as an alternative batching method.

parsed.summary: This lecture page details the computational challenges of training Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), specifically the graph expansion problem where receptive fields grow exponentially with depth. It compares three optimization strategies: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Batch Gradient Descent, and Mini-batch Gradient Descent, highlighting the trade-offs in memory usage, convergence stability, and computational efficiency. The page introduces GraphSAGE as a solution for scalable training through random neighborhood sampling and discusses graph partitioning as an alternative batching method.
